c.tagline: Motor City reborn - Motown, techno, Art Deco towers, and a riverfront rising.

taxi.fareNote: Street cabs are uncommon; most visitors rely on Uber and Lyft, which are widely available across the metro area.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Downtown/Midtown revitalized and safe; many outer neighborhoods high-crime — stay central

hood_desc: The revitalized core around Campus Martius Park, with skyscrapers, sports arenas, casinos, and the riverfront; the most convenient and walkable base for a first Detroit visit.
Detroit's cultural heart, home to the Detroit Institute of Arts, the Charles H. Wright Museum, Wayne State University, and a growing dining scene; ideal for museum-goers and culture seekers.

Detroit's oldest neighborhood, now its trendiest, with Michigan Central Station's grand revival, buzzing bars, farm-to-table restaurants, and vintage shops; suits hip travelers who want character and nightlife.
A compact entertainment strip of Greek restaurants, a casino, and bars beside the historic district; lively day and night and popular with visitors who want dining and gaming within walking distance.
A quieter, architecturally rich area anchored by the Art Deco Fisher Building and the original Motown Museum (Hitsville U.S.A.); good for those who want history and calm just north of the action.
lodging: Aloft Detroit at The David Whitney

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink and meets federal standards.

transit.pay: Buy a DART card or use the DART mobile app to ride DDOT and SMART buses; the base bus fare is $2.00 and a DART day pass is $5. The QLINE streetcar along Woodward Avenue and the downtown People Mover both currently run fare-free.
transit.hours: DDOT runs 24 hours on several core routes; the QLINE runs roughly 6am to midnight (later on weekends), and the People Mover runs from morning until around midnight.

air: Coleman A. Young International Airport (DET, general aviation)
train: Detroit Amtrak Station (New Center, Wolverine line)

transit.m: SMART FAST Michigan bus to downtown Detroit (~45-60 min)

tip.r: ~15-20% is standard at restaurants; round up for taxis and tip $1-2 per drink at bars.

food.name: Coney dog
food.desc: Natural-casing beef frank in a steamed bun under beanless chili, yellow mustard and diced raw onion; a Detroit fixture for over a century.

places.name: American Coney Island
places.note: Open since 1917 and still 24 hours; one half of the city's famous side-by-side rivalry.

places.name: Lafayette Coney Island
places.note: The scruffier next-door rival that many Detroiters swear is the better of the two.

places.name: Duly's Place
places.note: Tiny 24-hour counter beloved by locals for a less touristy coney.

food.name: Detroit-style square pizza
food.desc: Thick, airy pan pizza baked in blue steel trays so the brick cheese caramelises into a crisp frico edge, with sauce ladled on top.

places.name: Buddy's Pizza
places.area: Conant St at Six Mile, original location
places.note: Where the style was invented in 1946; the original bar is still the pilgrimage stop.

places.name: Loui's Pizza
places.note: Chianti-bottle-draped local legend often cited as the best square pizza in metro Detroit.

places.name: Michigan & Trumbull
places.note: Modern Corktown pizzeria giving the Detroit square a gourmet, ingredient-driven update.

food.name: Shawarma and Lebanese mezze
food.desc: Slow-roasted spit meat shaved into house-baked bread, eaten with hummus, fattoush and garlic toum in America's largest Arab-American community.

places.name: Al Ameer
places.note: James Beard America's Classics winner; the region's benchmark for Lebanese cooking.

places.name: Hamido Restaurant
places.note: Busy Dearborn favourite for charcoal-grilled meats and generous mezze spreads.

places.name: Bucharest Grill
places.note: Detroit institution that sells thousands of shawarma wraps a week, late into the night.

food.name: Paczki
food.desc: Dense Polish filled doughnuts of prune, rose or custard, fried in vast numbers for Fat Tuesday in Hamtramck's bakeries.

places.name: New Palace Bakery
places.note: Old-school Polish bakery whose Paczki Day queues stretch around the block.

places.name: New Martha Washington Bakery
places.note: Neighbourhood Polish bakery selling paczki and rye breads year-round.

places.name: Srodek's Quality Sausage
places.note: Polish deli and market stocking paczki alongside its own kielbasa.

food.name: Corned beef egg rolls
food.desc: A pure Detroit invention: corned beef, swiss and sauerkraut wrapped in an egg roll skin, deep fried and dipped in thousand island.

places.name: Cutter's Bar & Grill
places.note: Widely credited with popularising the corned beef egg roll; a market-day institution.

places.name: Mudgie's Deli
places.note: Well-loved Corktown sandwich shop with a strong corned beef program.

places.name: Eastern Market vendors
places.note: Weekend food stalls around the sheds turn out their own versions.

food.name: Polish pierogi and kielbasa
food.desc: Potato-and-cheese or kraut dumplings pan-fried in butter with onions, served with smoked kielbasa and dill pickle soup.

places.name: Polish Village Cafe
places.note: Basement dining room serving huge plates of pierogi and kielbasa for decades.

places.name: Srodek's Quality Sausage
places.note: Sausage maker and deli where locals buy pierogi by the dozen to take home.

places.name: Eastern Market sheds
places.note: Polish meat and dumpling vendors among the Saturday market stalls.

food.name: Boston cooler
food.desc: Despite the name, a Detroit original: Vernors ginger ale, brewed here since 1866, blended with vanilla ice cream into a spicy float.

places.name: Sanders Chocolate & Ice Cream Shoppe
places.note: Detroit confectionery institution since 1875; the classic soda-fountain setting.

places.name: Ray's Ice Cream
places.note: Long-running metro Detroit scoop shop that blends the float to order.

places.name: American Coney Island
places.note: Vernors on tap to wash down the coneys, the traditional pairing.

food.name: Detroit craft beer
food.desc: The city's brewing revival runs from Corktown taprooms to Rivertown warehouses, with strong local ales, lagers and Michigan-hopped IPAs.

places.name: Batch Brewing Company
places.note: Neighbourhood brewpub with rotating small batches and a community-focused kitchen.

places.name: Motor City Brewing Works
places.note: One of Detroit's original craft breweries, with wood-fired pizza to match.

places.name: Atwater Brewery
places.note: Established Detroit brewery and beer hall in a converted riverside warehouse.

landmarks: Renaissance Center
The gleaming cylindrical glass towers of GM's headquarters dominate the Detroit riverfront skyline.
Michigan Central Station
The monumental Beaux-Arts former train station, recently restored by Ford, is a powerful symbol of Detroit's revival.
Belle Isle Park
This island park's James Scott Memorial Fountain and conservatory provide lush, scenic riverside photo settings.
The Spirit of Detroit
This large bronze civic statue outside the Coleman A. Young Municipal Center is an enduring city emblem.
Fox Theatre
The ornate 1928 movie palace's lavish marquee and interior make it one of downtown's most photogenic landmarks.
Detroit Institute of Arts
Home to Diego Rivera's famed Detroit Industry murals, the DIA's grand Beaux-Arts facade is a cultural icon.
Guardian Building
Nicknamed the 'Cathedral of Finance,' this Art Deco skyscraper features a dazzling colorful tiled lobby.
Ambassador Bridge
This suspension bridge linking Detroit to Windsor, Canada is an iconic feat of engineering over the river.
Comerica Park
Home of the Detroit Tigers, this ballpark's giant tiger statues and Ferris wheel give it a distinct visual identity.
Eastern Market
One of the oldest and largest public markets in the US, known for its vibrant murals and bustling market sheds.

train.note: Windsor, Ontario is visible across the river, but no passenger train crosses - the Detroit River rail tunnel carries freight only, so for VIA Rail you have to reach Windsor station by road first. Amtrak's Wolverine runs about three times a day from the compact New Center station on Woodward Avenue, roughly three miles north of downtown, calling at Ann Arbor, Jackson, Kalamazoo and Chicago in around five and a half hours. The Blue Water and Pere Marquette serve other Michigan corridors but not Detroit itself. The station is a small modern building with limited facilities, so arrive shortly before departure rather than early.

bus.note: Transit Windsor's cross-border Tunnel Bus, for decades the cheap way between downtown Detroit and Windsor, was cancelled in 2025, so there is currently no scheduled international coach; crossing now means a taxi or rideshare through the Detroit-Windsor Tunnel or over the Ambassador Bridge, with a passport, enhanced licence or NEXUS card. Domestically, Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/), FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) and Megabus (https://us.megabus.com/) run to Chicago (about five to six hours), Cleveland, Toledo, Ann Arbor and Grand Rapids. Indian Trails (https://www.indiantrails.com/) covers the rest of Michigan including the Upper Peninsula. Book online for the lowest fares.

ferry.note: Despite sitting on an international waterway, Detroit has no scheduled passenger ferry - the Detroit-Windsor crossing is by tunnel or bridge only. The boats on the river are the seasonal Detroit Princess dinner cruise and sightseeing charters. The nearest working ferries are small crossings further downriver at Algonac and the seasonal boat to Boblo Island.

half.name: Ann Arbor
half.blurb: University of Michigan college town with a walkable downtown, museums, and a lively farmers market district.

half.name: Frankenmuth
half.blurb: Bavarian-themed Michigan town with half-timbered architecture, a riverboat cruise, and the sprawling Bronner's Christmas store.

half.name: Windsor
half.blurb: Ontario city just across the Detroit River, with a riverfront trail, a historic whisky distillery, and skyline views of Detroit.
